text:
incident-bot: PAGER - auth-proxy unusual traffic pattern: 401 spike from 3 external IPs, 6k reqs/min, potential token replay. Alert level: P1
mike_oncall: I’m on it, paging SRE and Sec. Taking ownership — will coordinate.
sara_sec: ack. Can we scope affected tokens/apps? initial hint: requests show header `x-auth-method: svc-token` and header snippet looks like `k8s-svc-...`
lee_sre: pulling logs from edge-proxy-2/edge-proxy-3 now, running `kubectl logs -n infra edge-proxy-2 --since=10m | grep auth` — will post samples.
mike_oncall: @sara_sec @lee_sre blocklist rule ready? If we can quickly block the top offending IPs at the LB layer, do it.
lee_sre: pushed ip deny for 3 ips (198.51.100.12, 203.0.113.7, 203.0.113.8) to fw-ops, confirm 198.51.100.12 now dropping.
sara_sec: good. Are tokens tied to a single service account? logs show `svcacct=inference-batcher` in 48% of hits.
olivia_support: CS: we have 2 customer tickets about 502/503 at 02:16 UTC, likely related. Flagging for comms.
mike_oncall: initial impact: 2 customers degraded, internal error spike in gen-api routes. Prioritize mitigation then comms.
sara_sec: recommend immediate rotation for `inference-batcher` keys and revocation of active sessions. Can Security trigger KMS rotation and create short-lived keys?
jordan_pmgr: I can prep a customer notice draft once we have confirmed scope and ETA.
lee_sre: running one-off revoke with admin tool: `POST /admin/revoke?svc=inference-batcher` — started 02:20 UTC. Expect session flush within 30s.
lee_sre: sample log: `2026-03-20T02:18:22Z auth=svc-token svcacct=inference-batcher ip=203.0.113.7 status=200 token_id=tok_abc123 replay_score=0.95`
sara_sec: high replay_score suggests token reuse. Also found one log with `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.12, 10.0.0.5` i.e., suspicious spoofing.
mike_oncall: decide: rotate keys for `inference-batcher` and enforce short-lived TTL on new tokens. Anyone object?
olivia_support: no objections. CS: we should give affected customers an interim note: "we’re investigating auth anomalies, mitigation in progress, expect rotation within 15–30m" — draft incoming.
lee_sre: rotation script running: `/opt/tools/rotate_svc_keys --svc inference-batcher --kms alias/redwood/infra` — started 02:24 UTC.
sara_sec: after rotation, enable stricter `token-ttl` to 5m and require mTLS between services for svc tokens.
mike_oncall: action list: 1) Block offending IPs (done). 2) Revoke inference-batcher sessions (in progress). 3) Rotate keys (in progress). 4) Tighten TTL + mTLS (pending). 5) Draft customer comms (jordan/olivia). 6) Post-incident forensics (sara/lee).
olivia_support: draft note: "At 02:15 UTC we observed anomalous authentication traffic affecting some inference requests. We've blocked suspicious sources and rotated affected service keys. We're investigating root cause; no customer data leakage confirmed so far." Want approval to send.
sara_sec: ok to send interim notice, include guidance: customers should rotate their own external service credentials if they used any public keys we manage (rare). Also include contact for security followup.
lee_sre: rotation completed 02:28 UTC. New keys issued and hot-swapped. Preliminary metrics: auth failures down to baseline in 60s after swap.
mike_oncall: thanks. Jordan/Olivia please send interim update. Tagging @exec-alert if customer impact grows.
jordan_pmgr: sending now. will attach known affected customer IDs privately.
olivia_support: sent to impacted customers and CS channel. repeating: no confirmed data exfil so far.
sara_sec: keep kernel of evidence: saved packet captures and audit logs to `s3://rdw-incidents/2169999999/` — do not share externally. Created a findings-ticket: #INC-2169999999.
lee_sre: will follow up with deeper logs (edge traces, token issue times). plan to run replay detection across last 24h.
mike_oncall: plan for next 2h: finish forensics, prepare postmortem with timeline, confirm if any infra misconfig allowed token reuse. If anything else, call pager.
incident-bot: Note: incident P1 recorded and assigned to mike_oncall.
mike_oncall: closing thread for now — all hands aware. Reopen if we see new anomalies. :thumbsup:
